html:
The Achuar are an Indigenous people of the Amazon who speak a Jivaroan language, alongside the Shuar, the Shiwiar, the Awajún and the Wampis. They live along the Pastaza, Morona and Corrientes rivers in the rainforest on both sides of the border of Ecuador and Peru.

They live in scattered large houses, farm manioc in forest gardens, hunt with blowguns and fish. Dreams and visions guide daily decisions. The Achuar were among the last peoples of the region to meet outsiders, with lasting contact only from the 1960s and 1970s.

In Peru oil companies drilled on their land along the Corrientes from the 1970s, and spills polluted rivers and fish. In Ecuador the Achuar have refused oil drilling and set up ecotourism instead. See also Shuar and Wampis.
